title: Stack Filtering: Elevating Precision and Efficiency in Rust Pointer Analysis
problem: Context-sensitive pointer analysis generates excessive spurious points-to relations involving variables pointing to stack objects beyond their lifetimes, harming both efficiency and precision in Rust program analysis.
motivation: Rust's automatic memory management and stack-first allocation strategy create opportunities to prune invalid points-to relations; improving analysis precision is critical for Rust verification.
method: Stack filtering uses Rust's stack object lifetime information in two phases: (1) assess stack object liveness via function reachability and efficient call graph (RTA), (2) filter out points-to relations involving inactive stack objects during context-sensitive analysis. Integrated into Ruypē pointer analysis framework.
key_novelty: Leveraging Rust's explicit stack object lifetimes to prune spurious context-sensitive points-to relations without full flow-sensitivity.
contributions: Stack filtering technique using stack object liveness
Integration into Rust context-sensitive pointer analysis
Reduced analysis time and memory consumption while improving precision
limitations: Specific to Rust language and stack allocation model; generalization to other languages not discussed.
primary_theme: Rust-specific pointer analysis precision via stack filtering
